observations: Photo 0 shows a Nikon-branded box with large printed text that appears to read “D750”. A DSLR camera body is visible on top of the box.
Photo 1 shows the inside of a Nikon packaging box with manuals/leaflets; the visible text on the box area includes “D750”.
Photo 2 shows the camera body wrapped in bubble wrap inside the carton; no clear model number is readable on the camera itself.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 show Nikon packaging text that appears to be “D750”.
Photos mainly show packaging and wrapped items; no close-up of the body condition (scratches, sensor dust, wear) is shown.
No powered-on screen, shutter test, or functional demo is shown in the photos.

claims.claim: We have The model is D850.
claims.evidence: Seller text says D850, but photos show “D750” on the Nikon packaging (photo 0 and photo 1).

risks.risk: Model mismatch risk (seller says D850 but photos show D750 packaging). Buying the wrong body is the biggest risk to price.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the camera’s model marking on the body (or the menu “About/Model” screen) with the screen readable.
risks.if_unproven: Price as the worst-case matching the photos: Nikon D750 body (not D850).

risks.risk: Not actually tested/working risk (no proof the shutter, autofocus, buttons, and sensor are functional).
risks.proof: Ask for a short video: power on, show live view, take 3 shots, and show the shutter count or at least a successful capture on the screen.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed working (worst-case: treat as needing testing/possible faults).

risks.risk: Condition risk (could be heavily used despite “as new” claim; photos don’t show the exterior closely).
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of: front/back, mount area, buttons/dials, and any visible scratches/dents.

risks.risk: Accessories/what’s included risk (body-only vs includes battery/charger/strap).
risks.proof: Ask for a full contents photo laid out: battery, charger, cables, strap, manuals, and whether it’s body-only.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the camera body showing the exact model (or a readable menu screen showing the model).
Video proof of operation: power on + live view + take a few shots + confirm images appear on the screen.
Close-up exterior condition photos (front/back, lens mount, top dials/buttons).
Photo of everything included (battery, charger, strap, cables) to confirm whether it’s body-only.
response.reason: The seller’s text conflicts with the photos (D850 claimed vs D750 shown on packaging), and there is no functional proof that the camera is working or what accessories are included—so a safe price cannot be selected from the comparables without the decisive model/working confirmation.
